WORKSHOP AND TRANSPORT RECORDS — BURAK YÜCEL

SEARCH RESULT: 1 RECORD.

14 November 2006, around 00.40. Bakırköy, Sahil Student Residence (construction unfinished, partly in use).

Umut Yücel (19) was found in the building’s stairwell, having fallen from the third-floor landing; he was taken to hospital and could not be saved. The ambulance call was made at 01.22.

The file was closed as ‘accidental death’. Grounds: influence of alcohol, unfinished stair railing, consistency of witness statements.

Building owner: Saran İnşaat (Nevzat Saran).

File document list:
1. Scene report — in file
2. Witness statements (5 people) — in file
3. Scene photographs (12) — NOT IN FILE
4. Floor attendant’s statement — NOT IN FILE
5. Ambulance call record — in file
The closed death file from 2006 was taken out of the archive and added to your investigation.
2006 INCIDENT RECORD — SAHIL STUDENT RESIDENCE
Statement of the victim of Incident C.
Old things. Letters and photographs from my student years. Nothing valuable. I don’t know why they took it.
As she said ‘nothing valuable’ she turned her eyes to the window.
What was in the box?
I don’t remember. Really.
In Bakırköy, near the seafront, in a student residence that had just opened. The building wasn’t finished yet; the scaffolding was still up. We stayed a year. Then it closed.
Where did you live as a student?

The light was on in the study. I opened the door and someone was there. Masked, wearing a cap. They lunged at me, I fell, I grabbed an arm, they pushed me. They got out over the balcony. I didn’t see the face.
Touched the bandage on her forehead.
What happened when you went into the flat?
…We stayed in the same residence. Years ago. We don’t see each other.
Spoke after a long silence.
Do you know Selim Arca or Tolga Saran?
“Umut had been drinking.”
Assoc. Prof. Aylin Karataş — interview
Interview held after the archive record.
Umut’s notes. And a small cassette. The tape from the voice recorder Umut carried everywhere. It fell out of his pocket that night; I took it. I never listened to it. I couldn’t.
What was really in the box?
Umut had been drinking. …He’d had two glasses. I don’t know. We all said so.
Had Umut been drinking?
…I heard it. I heard it, yes. I’ve been hearing it for twenty-two years. We all say ‘we found out the next morning’; that’s how we talked. It became a habit.
Her eyes filled, but her voice did not break.
You told us ‘I found out about it the next morning’. In 2006 you said ‘I heard the sound of the fall’.
Assoc. Prof. Aylin Karataş — second interview
No one… Only Zeynep. Last month she called to talk about something that had come to Selim; we talked. I told her, ‘I’ve still got the box.’ I don’t know why I told her.
After saying it she raised her hand to her mouth.
Who knew you had kept the box?

No. I dropped the envelope through the letterbox in the afternoon and left. In the evening I was at the workshop. I didn’t touch anyone. I sent the envelopes. I wanted them to be scared. I did nothing else.
Raised his voice for the first time.
Did you also get into Aylin Karataş’s home?
Statement of Burak Yücel, located in Kadıköy.
I don’t know. I only know about the envelopes.

Yes. I had the negative; twenty-two years. I cut it into three, one piece for each of them. I typed it on my mother’s old typewriter. Its ‘a’ is faulty. I wanted them to be scared. To tell it, just once.
Folded his arms and never unfolded them.
Did you send the envelopes?
Yes. I thought if I left the envelope at his door he’d throw it away. I wanted him to find it on his seat. I didn’t take anything.
Did you also break the window of Tolga Saran’s car?
“I wanted them to be scared. I did nothing else.”

ENVELOPE C — CONTENTS
The report repeated the conclusion of the old file. The sentence learned by heart twenty-two years ago went on record once more, this time with your signature.

The report wrote that Tolga pushed Umut down. When the cassette and Ferhat’s statement showed Umut got up and walked away after being pushed, that part fell apart; the reopening of the old file was delayed too.

The report reconstructed the 2006 incident without reducing it to a single culprit’s push: a fight, a push, half an hour later a staircase without a railing, and then forty minutes of silence. The Umut Yücel file was set aside to be reopened as a separate investigation.
The 2006 incident was left undetermined. The cassette stayed in the file; nobody applied for it to be reopened.

Burak Yücel gave a statement on charges of making threats and criminal damage; the typewriter and the negative were handed over. For the first time he made a formal application regarding his brother’s file.
The charge brought against Tolga Saran had no basis.
The source of the envelopes remained open.
Pinning the envelopes on Zeynep collapsed with Burak’s confession; the file came back.

On the morning of 9 November, Tolga Saran (40), who lives in Bakırköy, reported that the front passenger window of his car, parked in the estate’s open-air car park, had been broken during the night. Nothing was stolen from the car.

A sealed brown envelope was found on the driver’s seat. The envelope has been recorded separately.

The incident has been opened as a separate criminal damage record.
INCIDENT RECORD B — CAR WINDOW BROKEN

On the evening of 10 November, Assoc. Prof. Aylin Karataş (42), who lives in Bakırköy, came home and encountered someone inside; a brief struggle took place. The attacker escaped through the balcony door.

Aylin Karataş was treated for minor injuries to her arm and forehead. No valuables were taken from the home; an old cardboard box is missing from the study.

A brown envelope was found in the pile of post inside the front door. The incident was routed to this desk as it was seen to be similar in nature to the merged file.

Burak described sending the envelopes, keeping the negative and cutting it into three, and the typewriter with the faulty ‘a’; the person in the car park record leaves alone and takes nothing.
Tolga was one of the people who received an envelope; there is no basis for him being the same person who sent them.
The source of the envelopes could be determined from Burak’s statement and the typewriter marks.
Zeynep was on the side that feared the envelopes. The envelopes were typed and made from the negative; Burak has both.

Zeynep said, ‘Nobody call anyone.’ Tolga called his father. Nevzat Bey came, with his men. He told us what to say, one by one. ‘He’d had a lot to drink; nobody touched him.’ They only called the ambulance after they arrived. Forty minutes.
His voice shook.
What happened after he fell?
Statement of one of the 2006 witnesses, taken by phone.

Umut’s brother. Burak. He was fifteen; he’d come to see his big brother, he had a camera. In the late afternoon he lined us all up. He must have kept the negatives. I heard he works at a print workshop in Kadıköy now.
Who took the photograph?
I wouldn’t know. I broke off with those people long ago.
I said it. They made me say it. Nobody asked me ‘really?’. I’ve been waiting for this conversation for twenty-two years.
For a long time only his breathing could be heard.
You said you went to bed early that night.
“I’ve been waiting for this conversation for twenty-two years.”
Ferhat Tunç — interview

Tolga and Umut fought on the top floor. Umut was going to write about his father’s building, for a newspaper. Tolga pushed him; Umut hit the iron of the railing. But he didn’t fall; he got up, said ‘I’m fine’ and went downstairs crying. Half an hour later we heard the scream. The stairs had no railing; it was dark. Tolga wasn’t there at that moment. Nobody pushed him down. But if Tolga hadn’t pushed him, he wouldn’t have gone down those stairs in that state.
What did you see?

Statement of the person who reported Incident A.
I don’t know that. As a doctor, that’s all I can say.
No. My patients like me. I have no debts, no lawsuits. Look, I put this on record because my wife insisted. A bad joke.
Is there anyone who has a problem with you?
In Istanbul. I studied medicine, lived in a residence, then specialist training. Like everyone.
Paused for a moment after saying ‘residence’.
Where did you spend your youth?
No. A building, a few shoulders. It could be anywhere. I think someone found it somewhere and sent it at random.
Answered without looking at the photocopy.
Do you recognise the photograph?
“A bad joke. I don’t have a problem with anyone.”
Dr. Selim Arca — interview
Interview held after the archive record.
It was an accident. The stairs had no railing. Everyone knows that.
What happened that night?
…I’d left around nine. I mean… I was there that evening, then I went down to my room. It’s been twenty-two years. I mix up the times.
Went back and forth between ‘I’d left’ and ‘I went down to my room’.
You implied to us that you weren’t at the residence that night. In 2006 you said ‘I saw Umut on the top floor at 22.30’.
Dr. Selim Arca — second interview
Because it was true. We all saw the same thing.
His voice was flat as he said it; as if learned by heart.
Four people used the same sentence: ‘He’d had a lot to drink. Nobody touched him.’

The three photograph pieces and the same faulty typewriter tied the envelopes together; the joined photograph opened the 2006 record. The shared sentence in the old statements and today’s contradictions revealed an aligned account. The barrier record, the phone location and the earring placed Zeynep at Aylin’s home; the box found in the car search and the matching earring tied her to the break-in. Burak’s workshop records separated the sender of the envelopes from the person who entered the home. The cassette and Ferhat told how, in 2006, the push was not the fall.

One file can hold more than one culprit and more than one crime: the envelopes, the break-in and twenty-two years of silence came from different hands. Separating is as much the work of an investigation as linking.
Bakırköy — 6–10 November 2028 · Sahil Student Residence, 14 November 2006

On the night of 14 November 2006, at the unfinished Sahil Student Residence, Umut Yücel fought with Tolga Saran after saying he would write about Saran İnşaat’s building. Tolga pushed him; Umut hit the railing but got up and went down the stairs. Half an hour later he fell from the landing that had no railing. Zeynep said ‘Nobody call anyone’, Tolga called his father Nevzat Saran; the ambulance was called forty minutes later and the statements were reduced to a single sentence. Twenty-two years later, Burak, the brother who had taken the photograph, cut the negative into three and sent the pieces to Selim, Tolga and Aylin. Zeynep, who knew her own voice was on the cassette, had learned that Aylin had kept the box; on the evening of 10 November she broke into the home, took the box and escaped by pushing Aylin, who had come home early.
Who sent the envelopes?

My father got everything sorted. That night… of course he came; it was his building. His lawyers came too. They were there until morning.

I was going to say I’d long since left the building… Look, my father was building that residence. Of course I was there too. When it happened I was on the floor below.
